t.d: Hand-making of turn-shoe pointe shoes with paste-hardened blocks, each maker identified by a personal mark.
t.tech: turn-shoe construction sewn inside out, block built from layers of paper, card and hessian with flour paste, baked overnight
t.mat: satin, paper, card, hessian, flour paste, leather sole
ctr: Freed of London, St Martin's Lane shop and Hackney factory
t.auth: maker's symbol stamped on the sole (e.g. Crown, Wine Glass, Fish); no wood in the block

t.d: Hand-carved and painted wooden waterfowl and shorebird decoys, made for gunning and later as decorative bird carving.
t.tech: hand carving and painting of wooden bird forms
ctr: A. Elmer Crowell (East Harwich, Massachusetts, active 1912–1952)
Lem and Steve Ward, Crisfield style (Crisfield, Maryland)
t.auth: attribution to a named carver; Crowell pieces before the late 1920s are rated above later output; Crowell's preening pintail and Canada goose share the $1.13 million auction record

t.d: Local craftsmen shape hurleys from ash, using the butt of the tree near the root.
t.tech: sawing and shaping ash planks; steel band on the bas; splicing repairs
t.auth: cut from the root end of an ash butt

t.d: Workshop tradition that formalised Japanese wooden-sword making; four workshops remain.
t.mat: white oak, red oak, biwa, buna

t.d: Hand-building fishing rods from strips of split bamboo planed to a taper and glued into a hexagonal or other section.
t.tech: splitting culms into triangular strips, planing tapers to 0.001 in, gluing six strips, silk whipping, varnishing
t.mat: Tonkin cane, silk thread, varnish, cork grip, wood reel seat, metal ferrules
t.auth: maker's stamps and signatures; patent and registration marks date a rod; original bag and labels

t.d: Building of Davos and Grindelwald wooden sledges from steam-bent ash with metal-shod runners.
t.tech: steam bending, hand shaping of runners, screwed metal shoeing
t.auth: slatted ash seat on bent ash runners with screwed metal shoes; maker's mark

t.r: England (willow from Essex and East Anglia; workshops in Sussex and Nottingham)
t.d: Making cricket bats from cleft English cricket bat willow, pressed and hand-finished.
t.tech: butt cut to length and split into clefts · dried · pressed · cane handle spliced in · hand shaped, balanced and polished
t.mat: cricket bat willow (Salix alba var. caerulea), cane handle
ctr: J S Wright (Great Leighs, Essex; willow supplier)
t.auth: Straight, even grains (about 8–12 visible) on the face; English and Kashmir willow are the same species, so origin cannot be told reliably from the wood.
